author: Elastic
attributes.description: Flags an existing Role or ClusterRole being changed (patch or update) to a wildcard on every API resource and verb. This may be indicative of a deliberate privilege expansion but may also be a nefarious attempt at privilege escalation.
false_positives: Platform installers, GitOps controllers, and emergency break-glass roles sometimes ship or widen wildcard ClusterRoles; correlate with change records and narrow by user or service account when baselined.
attributes.name: AWS EKS RBAC Wildcard Elevation on Existing Role
attributes.note:
## Triage and analysis

### Investigating AWS EKS RBAC Wildcard Elevation on Existing Role
Someone patched or updated a Role or ClusterRole so the stored rules grant star verbs and star resources—near
cluster-admin breadth on that scope. Confirm the actor (user, group, impersonation), client, and non-loopback source
IP; then see who can bind that role.

### Possible investigation steps

- Diff the role YAML before and after; list RoleBindings and ClusterRoleBindings that reference it and which subjects
  gained the widened access.
- In the same window, check secret reads, exec, and further RBAC changes from the same identity.

### False positive analysis

- Approved GitOps or vendor upgrades sometimes widen a known ClusterRole; allowlist stable automation when documented.

### Response and remediation

- Revert the role, drop unexpected bindings, rotate credentials for the actor, and block future wildcard RBAC outside
  governed pipelines (policy-as-code, PR-only RBAC).
attributes.query:
from logs-aws.eks_audit-* metadata _id, _index, _version
| where
  aws.eks.audit.objectRef.resource in ("roles", "clusterroles") and
  aws.eks.audit.verb in ("update", "patch") and
  `aws.eks.audit.annotations.authorization_k8s_io/decision` == "allow" and
  aws.eks.audit.level == "RequestResponse" and
  aws.eks.audit.stage == "ResponseComplete" and
  aws.eks.audit.sourceIPs is not null and
  not aws.eks.audit.sourceIPs in ("::1", "127.0.0.1") and
  KQL(""" aws.eks.audit.responseObject.rules.verbs:"*" and aws.eks.audit.responseObject.rules.resources:"*" """)
| keep user.name, user_agent.original, event.action, source.ip, aws.eks.audit.verb, aws.eks.audit.objectRef.resource, aws.eks.audit.objectRef.name, aws.eks.audit.requestURI, aws.eks.audit.user.username, aws.eks.audit.user.groups, `aws.eks.audit.annotations.authorization_k8s_io/decision`, event.original, _id, _version, _index, data_stream.namespace
attributes.setup:
This rule reads EKS control-plane audit logs collected by the AWS integration
into `logs-aws.eks_audit-*`, where the AWS EKS audit ingest
pipelines normalize each audit record under `aws.eks.audit.*`.

Enable the `audit` control-plane log type on the EKS cluster, send its
CloudWatch log group through the AWS integration, and confirm events carry
`data_stream.dataset: aws.eks_audit` and
`cloud.provider: aws` before enabling this rule.
tags: Data Source: Kubernetes API Server Audit Logs
